title: Getting Started
text: This guide will help you get started with ColorVintner.

title: Installation
text:
First, install the package: using Pkg
Pkg.add("ColorVintner")

title: Basic Usage
text:
Load the package and start exploring: using ColorVintner

# See all available schemes
show_all_scheme_names()

title: Get Information About a Specific Scheme
text:
# Get detailed information about a scheme
colors = list_scheme_colors_in_rbg(:Blues_5) This will show you: The scheme nameNumber of colors in the schemeHex color codes for each color

title: Get All Schemes as a DataFrame
text:
# Create a DataFrame with all schemes
df = list_schemes_colors_in_hex()
first(df, 10)  # Show first 10 schemes

title: Basic Color Bar Plot
text:
# Plot a few schemes
plot_color_bars([:Blues_5, :Reds_5, :Greens_5])

title: Custom Plot Settings
text:
# Plot with custom settings
plot_color_bars([:Blues_5, :Reds_5, :Greens_5], 
                schemes_per_row=3, 
                save_path="my_plot.pdf",
                plot_title="My Color Schemes")

title: Comprehensive Visualization
text:
# Create all category plots and save to a directory
plots = plot_schemes_by_category(save_dir="./color_plots")

title: Sequential Schemes
text:
Use for data that progresses from low to high values: # Examples of sequential schemes
[:Blues_5, :Reds_5, :Greens_5, :Oranges_5]

title: Diverging Schemes
text:
Use for data with a meaningful center point: # Examples of diverging schemes
[:RdBu_5, :PiYG_5, :BrBG_5, :PuOr_5]

title: Qualitative Schemes
text:
Use for categorical data: # Examples of qualitative schemes
[:Set1_5, :Set2_5, :Set3_5, :Paired_5]

title: Get All Schemes
text: all_schemes = get_all_schemes()

title: Get Scheme Counts
text:
counts = get_scheme_count()
println("Total schemes: ", counts[:total])
println("Sequential: ", counts[:sequential])
println("Diverging: ", counts[:diverging])
println("Qualitative: ", counts[:qualitative])

title: Sequential Schemes
text: Sequential color schemes are designed for data that progresses from low to high values. They use a single hue that varies in lightness and saturation.

title: Diverging Schemes
text: Diverging color schemes are designed for data that has a meaningful center point (like zero). They use two different hues that meet at a neutral color.

title: Qualitative Schemes
text: Qualitative color schemes are designed for categorical data. They use distinct colors that are easily distinguishable from each other.
